stateDesignation.note: Conflicting. The previous edition recorded Washington ECS Level III, citing the WA DOH list (October 2024), and its review notes of 2026-07-04 (docs/IMPROVEMENTS-2026-07-03.md) report that the hospital's own site still claimed Level III while the May 2026 list did not show it; the 2025–2027 East Region plan appendix, which reproduces an earlier edition of the list, also names East Adams Rural Healthcare. Against that, the list as revised in May 2026 (DOH 345-299, read through search extracts in October 2026) omits it: the East-region rows returned Othello, Odessa, Ferry, Garfield, Lincoln, Newport, Mount Carmel, St. Joseph's Chewelah, Valley, Whitman, Pullman, Tri State, Deaconess, Holy Family and Sacred Heart, without East Adams. The list was read only through search extracts of an imperfectly extracted PDF, so that omission is not verified absence, and the hospital's own claim was not re-observed in this review. The hospital became a Rural Emergency Hospital in March 2026 (Spokesman-Review, 2026-04-23), ending inpatient care while keeping the emergency room, which may explain a change. Neither side is shown as settled; the Washington DOH settles its own categorization (open item). The East region is recategorized in ECS Round 2 (applications due 2026-11-24).

ed.note: Not confirmed: every source is from the hospital's opening in August 2025. A Pinedale Online guide published at the opening says the dedicated emergency room entrance is open 24/7 and tells people with stroke signs to come directly to it, and the News Letter Journal describes a four-bed emergency room; no source after the opening was found that states the emergency department or its hours (October 2026 search). An emergency department stated only at a hospital's opening stays unknown (METHODOLOGY section 2), as for Post Falls ER & Hospital. Its Critical Access Hospital status is not confirmed either (see the cah claim), so the CAH emergency-services requirement (42 CFR 485.618) does not settle it. A current source (the hospital's own page, the state licensing roster or CMS) would.
